newsitem.title: USA: Mexican seeds yield giant corn in Missouri garden.
newsitem.headline: Mexican seeds yield giant corn in Missouri garden.

text.p: A retired Missouri telephone worker said Friday he was baffled by the giant corn stalks that sprouted up in his vegetable garden after he planted Mexican seeds given to him by a neighbor.
Bob Ferguson, 66, said the sweetcorn stalks have topped out at between 15 and 17 feet -- nearly three times the size of normal corn plants.
"It was planted back in May and it just growed and growed and growed and growed," Ferguson said. "You can't believe it until you see it."
The nine rows of plants in his garden were just starting to put on ears, he said.
Ferguson theorized that the abundant rain and mild temperatures this summer in central Missouri agreed with the hybrid, which was probably more accustomed to Mexico's hot, dry climate.
